title: Affine charts of componentwise normalization
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], enumerate the finitely many minimal prime ideals of $A$ (a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime ideal) without repetitions as $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$. Put $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$, the field of fractions of the domain $A/\mathfrak p_i$, and let $B_i$ be its integral closure in $K_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. There are canonical isomorphisms of $U$-schemes $
u^{-1}(U)\simeq\coprod_{i=1}^t\operatorname{Spec}B_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{i=1}^t B_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Under these isomorphisms, the structural ring map is $A	o\prod_i B_i$, $a\mapsto(a mod\mathfrak p_i)_i$. If $U$ is empty then $t=0$, the product is the zero ring and the coproduct is the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), parts (1), (3), (4), and Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); the finite-product spectrum is the disjoint union of its factor spectra.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $A$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal] with ideal $(0)$ to obtain the finite set of minimal primes. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], the components of $U$ are precisely $V(\mathfrak p_i)$, with no repetitions. This justifies the indexing in the statement without any assumption of excellence or finiteness of normalization.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), proof of (1); Algebra Tags 00FR and 00ES

proof.text: The components $Z$ of $X$ meeting $U$ correspond bijectively to the components of $U$ by $Z\mapsto Z\cap U$. The cited [lem-sc-components-open-injection] supplies that this is an injective map into components of $U$. For surjectivity, a component $C$ of $U$ is irreducible also as a subset of $X$: any decomposition by closed subsets of $X$ restricts to one in $U$. Apply [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] to contain $C$ in a component $Z$ of $X$. Then $C\subseteq Z\cap U$, and maximality of $C$ and the first cited node give $C=Z\cap U$. Denote the unique component corresponding to $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ by $Z_i$.

source.place: Irreducible components and restriction to an open; applied to the component indexing in Morphisms Tag 0CDV

proof.text: Give each $Z_i$ its reduced induced structure. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], its restriction to $U$ is $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$: the radical ideal for $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ is $\mathfrak p_i$ itself. By [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], $Z_i$ is integral, and $W_i$ is a nonempty affine open of $Z_i$. Hence [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $k(Z_i)$ canonically with $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$ over $A/\mathfrak p_i$. In particular the inclusion of the affine coordinate ring into the function field is the one used to define $B_i$, rather than an arbitrary field identification.

source.place: Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); Schemes Tag 01J3 and Morphisms Tag 01RV

proof.text: Apply the explicit affine-chart construction in [def-fin-normalization-extension] to the integral scheme $Z_i$, its affine open $W_i$, and the degree-one finite extension $L=k(Z_i)$ of $k(Z_i)$. That node states both that $L=K$ is the function-field normalization and that its inverse image over an affine chart is the spectrum of the integral closure of the chart ring in $L$. With the field identification of Step 3 this gives $(Z_i^\nu)|_{W_i}=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with structural map induced by $A/\mathfrak p_i\to B_i$. Thus no finiteness of $B_i$ over $A/\mathfrak p_i$ is used.

source.place: Tag 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), affine integral-closure construction of Tag 035F (lemma-integral-closure), specialized to the generic point; compare Tag 035P

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], $X^
u$ is the disjoint union of the $Z^
u$ over all components $Z$ of $X$. The inverse image of $U$ in a summand is the inverse image of $Z\cap U$ under $Z^
u	o Z$; it is empty if $Z\cap U$ is empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the summands are disjoint open subschemes covering $X^
u$. Intersecting them with $
u^{-1}(U)$ leaves disjoint open subschemes with their restricted structure sheaves and still covers that inverse image. Therefore, using the indexing of Step 2 and the charts of Step 4, $
u^{-1}(U)\simeq\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. On the $i$-th summand the map to $U$ is the composite of the normalization map to $W_i$ with $W_i\hookrightarrow U$, hence is induced by $A	o A/\mathfrak p_i	o B_i$.

source.place: Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components), using the definition of componentwise normalization; restriction of a disjoint union

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to the finite family $(B_i)$. It supplies the second isomorphism, with the $i$-th coprojection induced by $\prod_jB_j\to B_i$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], morphisms between the affine schemes correspond contravariantly to ring maps. Consequently the ring map of the composite to $U$ has $i$-th coordinate $A\to A/\mathfrak p_i\to B_i$ by Step 5. A map into a product is determined by its coordinates, so it is exactly $a\mapsto(a\bmod\mathfrak p_i)_i$, followed in each coordinate by the canonical inclusion in $B_i$. The isomorphism is over $U$ for precisely this ring map.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), (3)-(4), with the finite-product-spectrum isomorphism in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Limits.lean, sigmaSpec

proof.text: If $U=\varnothing$, its coordinate ring is the zero ring by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (a sheaf of rings has the one-element ring of sections on the empty open). This ring has no proper prime ideals, so $t=0$. The empty product of rings is the one-element ring, whose spectrum has no points, and the empty coproduct of schemes is the empty scheme by the coproduct mapping property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Also $\nu^{-1}(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The unique ring map from the zero ring to the empty product is the stated map, so all previous identifications include this case.
